subject.title: [Feature]: First-class org/team deployment — workspace scaffolding, RBAC, and deployment manifests

question: Should OpenClaw core define first-class org/team deployment and RBAC as a supported security/config boundary, or keep the supported model as separate trusted Gateways plus narrower agent, binding, and sender-policy primitives?
rationale: The requested behavior would change Gateway auth, tool policy, session state, setup/config, and deployment guarantees, while current docs explicitly avoid hostile multi-tenant promises and VISION.md warns against heavy orchestration layers.

options.title: Decompose and keep umbrella
options.body: Keep this issue open as the parent and approve only scoped sub-issues for identity, RBAC, tenant isolation, scaffolding, manifests, and docs after the security boundary is chosen.

options.title: Route to narrower RFCs
options.body: Close this only after every remaining piece is represented by viable canonical issues such as per-session policy, tenant isolation, identity modes, and a separate scaffold/manifest item.

options.title: Decline core org deployment
options.body: Document separate Gateways, existing agent bindings, trusted proxy, and plugin/ClawHub tooling as the supported org deployment model instead of adding a first-class core surface.

recommendation.title: Decompose and keep umbrella
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the parent and approve only scoped sub-issues for identity, RBAC, tenant isolation, scaffolding, manifests, and docs after the security boundary is chosen.

likelyOwner.reason: The related conversation identity issue and adjacent security/config history make steipete the best available owner for this product/security boundary choice.
